core_obligations: Existence: define g on a fraction x/s by f(x) f(s) to the minus one, check it is a well-defined ring map from the definition of localisation, and note that the diagram commutes (proof lines 1314-1317).
Uniqueness: for any g' with g'(x/1) = f(x), use commutativity to get f(s) = g'(s/1), deduce g'(1/s) = f(s) to the minus one, and then compute g'(x/s) = g(x/s) (proof lines 1320-1324).
proof_roadmap: Define the map on fractions and verify well-definedness from the localisation construction (proof lines 1313-1317).
Show any commuting map agrees with it by computing on 1/s (proof lines 1319-1325).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that a ring map f from A to B sending every element of a multiplicative subset S to a unit factors uniquely through the localisation S^{-1}A (statement lines 1300-1311, with the commuting diagram drawn in the statement). The proof does not cite the universal property from elsewhere: it defines g on a fraction by f(x) f(s)^{-1}, notes that well-definedness follows from the definition of the localisation, and then proves uniqueness by computing the value of any competing map on 1/s and reducing a general fraction to a product (proof lines 1313-1325). The computation on 1/s is where the hypothesis that f inverts S is used, and the author writes both halves in full. H2.
